name: Stained glass
summary: Pieces of coloured glass held in lead strips, so that a window becomes a picture of coloured light.
how: Cut each piece to one colour; join the pieces with H-section lead 4 to 8 mm wide.
Paint the lines of faces and folds in dark grisaille and fire them onto the glass.
Use deep blue and red for the field; keep the clear or yellow pieces under 20% of the window.

origin.note: Abbot Suger consecrates the new choir of the Abbey of Saint-Denis, with tall windows of coloured glass.

adoptions.via: Victorian houses put coloured glass in doors, stair windows and fanlights.
Louis Comfort Tiffany and Jacques Gruber make leaded opalescent glass for lamps, ceilings and screens.

sources.title: Lawrence Lee, George Seddon and Francis Stephens, Stained Glass (1976)
